subject: Support for custom distributed computing platforms

messages.author: 521c7a73fe61d523
messages.subject: Support for custom distributed computing platforms
parts:
Hi,

I have my own distributed computing platform to which I can submit jobs and receive results.
How would irace be able to make use of it?

Currently, I have an exe that just runs an algorithm locally and prints the result on the commandline. I can however create any other exe, e.g. one that would submit the job, poll until the job is completed, download the job and print the result. Still, I am not sure if this would be a good way. It would certainly require some way of using batch mode in irace.

I also tried using "--parallel" option, but it results in an error:
Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :
  2 nodes produced errors; first error: could not find function "target.runner"
Calls: irace.cmdline ... clusterApplyLB -> dynamicClusterApply -> checkForRemoteErrors

My idea here was to use e.g. "--parallel 100" if I had 100 cores and I would expect irace to launch the executable maximum a hundred times (given that there are enough configurations alive).

Sincerely,
Andreas

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: Support for custom distributed computing platforms
parts:
Hi Andreas,

--batchmode only works if irace can run in the submission node and query the computing nodes for the status of jobs. You need to know the type of job scheduler and write a target-runner that submits jobs to the submission node. It is quite cumbersome to be honest. I'll be very happy to accept contributions if someone decided to improve it or move to something more advanced like: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/BatchJobs/index.html

--parallel without --batchmode should work almost everywhere. What you are seeing is a bug in Windows that will be fixed in irace 3.0. If you don't mind using a development version of irace, we can provide it to you.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: Support for custom distributed computing platforms
parts: On Wednesday, 11 April 2018 22:07:32 UTC+1, Don Beham wrote:

Hi,

I have my own distributed computing platform to which I can submit jobs and receive results.
How would irace be able to make use of it?

If you open the sources of irace and look in R/cluster.R, you can find the implementation for the various options of --batchmode. Basically, irace should be able to run in parallel in any platform on which R can run in parallel: https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/HighPerformanceComputing.html

It should run without problems in multiple CPUs of a single computer, but you may need to make some changes in irace if you want to run distributed across different computers and you are not using MPI, sge, pbs, torque or slurm

See section 6 of the user-guide for details.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.author: 521c7a73fe61d523
messages.subject: Re: Support for custom distributed computing platforms
parts:
Dear Manuel,

I took a look at the sources.

I think any cluster system could be more easily supported and readily out of the box if one could define three applications:
submit.exe - submits a job and returns the ID
stat.exe - checks whether the job ID is terminated
fetch.exe - fetches the job's results and outputs the cost (or fails if the job failed)

Currently, submit.exe can already be defined as target.runner and fetch.exe can be defined as target.evaluator.
However stat.exe cannot be parameterized because it's fixed to "qstat" and several out of the box supported cluster systems (SGE, TORQUE, etc.).

If you would add a "cluster.stat" parameter (pointing to an executable or script) in addition to "target.runner" and "target.evaluator" the out of the box supported cluster systems could become a configuration option and would not need to be hard-coded. In addition anybody can could use irace together with his or her cluster system. I assume there was a reason why qstat was hard-coded though.

Is there something else I am missing?

Sincerely,
Andreas

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] Re: Support for custom distributed computing platforms
parts:
Dear Andreas,

It sounds like a good idea and we can still keep the predefined modes and still
allow any other possible cluster system.

I'm happy to have a clusterStatus parameter that works like targetRunner (that
is, that can be a string pointing to an executable or an R function). If you
look at how targetRunner is used and documented in the code, it should be
obvious how to add such clusterStatus.

If you can provide a patch against the sources (for example, you can find a
read-only git repository of irace here: https://github.com/cran/irace), I'll be
more than happy to review it and integrate it in the next version (with due
credit in the NEWS, sources and user-guide). Unfortunately, Leslie and I are
too busy to implement this ourselves and we have a long TODO list of other
things that are more urgent.

Cheers,

Manuel.
